correctness.rationale: For any homeomorphism, an iterate preserves each chosen essential open edge; every orbit begun there has a subsequential limit in its closure. If that closure misses the target, a nonempty open positive-measure set misses the basin, ruling out both basin notions. Conversely, pull the target back to each parameterized closed edge, using two preimages of a loop vertex when needed. Gap maps are increasing, fix both endpoints, have the claimed sign of displacement, and fix at most one interior point per gap. The displacement bound yields continuity even at an accumulation of gaps. Gluing the maps and inverses gives a homeomorphism whose points not converging to the fixed target form a countable fixed set. For each neighborhood of any target point, either an interval is fixed within the neighborhood or a nonempty open interval flows to a gap endpoint in that neighborhood. This includes one-sided neighborhoods at vertices and the cut point of a circle. The resulting positive-measure, nonmeagre open witness excludes every competing closed set omitting that target point. Arc, circle and tripod consequences follow from the intrinsic edges. The mathematical proof, not the finite rational/decimal demonstrations, establishes the quantified assertion.
residual_risks: The conclusion does not cover infinite graphs or arbitrary measures. The recorded finite calculations are illustrations only.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Any missed essential edge eliminates an open set from the basin; a countable exceptional set is meagre; the previous proof's open failure-of-minimality witnesses exclude residual as well as full-measure basins. If a competing closed set is not contained in A, intersect it with A and use intersection of residual basins. The same realizer therefore gives generic minimality and simultaneous realization, including the circle case, without a new construction.

originality.rationale: The distinct indexed record 8d1440f91aeb states the same Milnor criterion under a weaker measure hypothesis and its actual proof yields the generic and simultaneous assertions as immediate consequences. Its necessity witness is an open edge; its realizing homeomorphism fixes the target, has only countably many fixed exceptions, and witnesses minimality on nonempty open sets. Replacing positive measure of a witness by nonmeagreness and nullity of the exceptions by meagreness gives the full generic clause for the very same map. The frozen cubic instead of split quadratics is a different formula but does not supply a distinct scientific outcome. There is demonstrable coverage; no publication order or priority is inferred from the shared date.
residual_risks: Priority between the same-day records is not resolved. An exhaustive search of older specialized graph-homeomorphism literature was not performed; it is not needed to establish the demonstrated coverage.

value.rationale: The intrinsically defined edge criterion is a meaningful structural answer to which closed sets can attract almost all and category-generic initial conditions on a branched graph. It handles arbitrary closed sets, not just finite examples, and can distinguish singleton realizability on graphs with different essential edge incidences. This is the mathematical value of the classification, not a claim of added value over the matching indexed result.
residual_risks: The modified interval formula alone has no established additional value over the indexed classification and construction.
